Victor Hugo, Notre-Dame de Paris, translated by Isabel F. Hapgood.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/victor-hugo/notre-dame-de-paris/isabel-f-hapgood

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Victor Hugo, the author, died 1885.
- Isabel F. Hapgood, the translator, died 1928.

First publication of the text used: 1888 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from French in 1888 by Isabel F. Hapgood.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1888, before 1931, so it is in the public domain in the United States. The edition's rights statement below says the same.
- Country of origin (not named in the facts; the translation is in English, so the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die, Isabel F. Hapgood (died 1928), means the translation is public domain in each of them from 1 January 1999 at the latest. The original French work by Victor Hugo is also public domain in every country, because its author died in 1925 or earlier.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Notre-Dame de Paris was published in 1831 by Victor Hugo. It was translated from French in 1888 by Isabel F. Hapgood.'
- Wikidata Q535 (Victor Hugo), P570 = 1885-05-22.
- Wikidata Q6077616 (Isabel F. Hapgood), P570 = 1928-06-26 and 1928-01-01.
